hints: Focus on structure and bonding across Period 3, metals conduct well, silicon conducts a little, and non-metals hardly conduct at all.
Check row 1 first, sodium is a giant metal, silicon is a semiconductor, and chlorine is a simple molecular insulator.
Now compare aluminium with magnesium and silicon with sulfur, remember conductivity follows number of mobile electrons, so link that to pick the rows that are in the correct greatest to least order.
walkthrough:
**Recall the conductivity trend in Period 3**

Think left to right. The metals Na, Mg, Al are good conductors due to delocalised electrons. Silicon is a metalloid semiconductor. P, S, Cl are molecular insulators with no mobile charge.

General order: $$\text{metals} > \text{Si} > \text{P, S, Cl (approx. zero)}$$

**Test row 1: sodium, silicon, chlorine**

Sodium is metallic with one mobile electron per atom, so high conductivity. Silicon conducts only slightly. Chlorine as $\text{Cl}_2$ molecules has no mobile electrons, so essentially zero.

Order $\text{sodium} > \text{silicon} > \text{chlorine}$ is correct.

**Test row 2: aluminium, magnesium, phosphorus**

Both Al and Mg are metals, but Al contributes 3 delocalised electrons per atom compared to 2 for Mg, so Al has the greater conductivity. Phosphorus ($\text{P}_4$) is an insulator.

Order $\text{aluminium} > \text{magnesium} > \text{phosphorus}$ is correct.

**Test row 3: sulfur, silicon, phosphorus**

Silicon is a semiconductor, so it must conduct better than sulfur. Sulfur as $\text{S}_8$ molecules is an insulator, just like phosphorus. Putting sulfur before silicon is backwards.

Row 3 is incorrect, so only rows 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: States row 1 only is correct. Row 1 is correct, but this misses that row 2 is also correct because aluminium conducts better than magnesium, and both conduct far better than phosphorus.
options.B: States rows 1 and 2 only are correct. Row 1 (Na > Si > Cl) and row 2 (Al > Mg > P) both follow the metals > metalloid > non-metal rule, while row 3 is wrong. This matches the analysis perfectly.
options.C: Includes row 3. Row 3 claims sulfur > silicon, which is backwards. Silicon is a semiconductor and sulfur is a molecular insulator with essentially zero conductivity, so this cannot be correct.
options.D: Includes all three rows. This is a trap if you think sulfur conducts because it is before chlorine or close to silicon. In fact silicon > sulfur, so row 3 fails and this option is wrong.
